messages:
maria: quick note from this morning's apples-to-apples run comparing KERNEL-Tuned-13B vs baseline-7B. we pinned decoding params and replayed the same prompts but saw a consistent p99 delta (~8%) on the smaller model. initial suspicion: kernel-bucket snapping + tokenizer trailing tokenization diffs.

devin: can you drop the exact replay command + flags so we can reproduce?

maria: pasted sanitized command below (sanitized paths):

```
./bin/replay_compare --replay s3://bench/replays/2026-03-18/seed-777 \\n  --model-primary kernel-tuned-13b:prod --model-secondary baseline-7b:prod \\n  --decoding \"temperature=0,top_p=0.95,max_new_tokens=64,stop=[\\\"\\\\n\\\",\\\"<END>\\\"]\" \\n  --batch-token-cap 2048 --kv-cache=on --log-kernel-selection \\n  --profile perf-bot --force-routing=auto
```

kai: two quick angles: (1) tokenization of trailing stop sequences can shift token alignment and force different attention kernel (fused vs unfused). (2) routing/batching heuristics: small-tail requests may be snapped into a low-latency path that uses a different kernel implementation. both change the compute mix.

andrew: for an apples-to-apples comparison we must assert token-id equality for prompt + first N tokens. otherwise we compare different code paths and it's meaningless. small snippet we use: 

```
ids_p = tok_p.encode(prompt).ids
ids_s = tok_s.encode(prompt).ids
if ids_p[:64] != ids_s[:64]: fail(\"token-id-mismatch\")
```

sophia: perf-bot output: baseline-7b shows ~10-12% more decode stalls and noticeable cudaMemcpy syncs during KV write on tail steps. KV memcpy time jumps on steps where batch occupancy <= 256 tokens.

perf-bot: summary (simplified):
decode_step_avg: 48.3ms vs 44.7ms (baseline-7b vs tuned-13b)
attention_fused_stall_pct: +13%
kv_write_memcpy_sync: observed on ~6% of steps (tail)
batch_occupancy_median: 960 tokens; tail mass at 64-256 tokens ~17%

maria: trace excerpt (stack names simplified):

```
decode_step: 52.1ms
  -> attention_fused: 27.9ms (warp_stalls +15%)
  -> mlp: 8.2ms
kv_cache_write: 5.6ms (memcpy_sync 5.0ms)
batch_merge_split: 5.4ms
```

devin: memcpy_sync on kv_write + skewed tail = classic small-batch memcpy domination. what's kernel-selection log show? are we switching fused kernel only for certain seqlen bucket?

maria: kernel-selection log attached (snippet):

```
step  1: seq_len_in_batch=512 -> kernel=fused_attention_v2
step 23: seq_len_in_batch=128 -> kernel=attention_fallback
step 54: seq_len_in_batch=1024 -> kernel=fused_attention_v2
```

kai: that snapping from fused->fallback will easily explain percent deltas. suggestion: rerun with experiments to isolate:
  1) replay with token-id equality assert + kv-cache=on (fail-fast)
  2) same but kv-cache=off to isolate decode-only cost
  3) synthetic generator that reproduces the exact token-length histogram and use --force-seqlen=512 to collapse kernel buckets
  4) replay with small-burst routing disabled to avoid tail diversion

andrew: include per-step kernel decision logs + routing reason code + batch occupancy histogram. we need to correlate kernel choices with memcpy sync events.

sophia: also normalize stop-seq canonicalization across tokenizers before runs. we had one case where \"\\n\" + \"<END>\" tokenized different between vocab variants and changed the effective max_new_tokens. that caused ~2-3% variance.

maria: implementing plan now. quick experimental note: i ran a sanity pass toggling kv-cache off and saw the p99 gap shrink to ~3% (so KV write/memcpy is significant but not whole story). rerunning with forced seqlen=512 next.

devin: good catch. when you post results, include the per-request token-id diffs (list of prompt ids that mismatched) and a sample of kernel-selection traces for those prompts.

maria: will do. ETA ~55m for full matrix (4 runs). kicking off jobs under perf-bot. job ids: 1798885001..1798885004.

perf-bot: scheduled jobs 1798885001-1798885004 started by maria

maria: started. will report back with concise tables (token-id parity count, p50/p95/p99 deltas, kernel-snap counts, memcpy-sync counts). ping me if you want any prompt subsets added.
